_doc: HMTc Category 10 (Infant and Child Durable Goods and Textiles, Ages 0-5) compiler config. Method v2.0, government-limit-only: every number is a regulatory lookup against a named row of data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, never an occurrence percentile, floor or precautionary adjustment. Twelve rows across three article families. EIGHT DURABLE-GOODS ROWS (cribs and bassinets, play yards and gates, strollers, walkers, swings and bouncers, infant carriers, high chairs and booster seats, car seats) are built on TOTAL ELEMENT CONTENT of each accessible component: the backbone is US CPSIA s.101 (100 mg/kg total lead in any part of a children's product) and 16 CFR 1303 (90 mg/kg in a surface coating), joined by Canada SOR/2018-83 (90 mg/kg in each accessible part of consumer products for the sleep, relaxation, hygiene, carrying or transport of children under four) and Canada SOR/2016-193 (90 mg/kg lead and 10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried surface coating material, and 90 mg/kg lead in applied stickers, films and coatings on furniture and products for children). THREE TEXTILE ROWS (clothing, bibs, blankets and sleep sacks) are built on the EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 EXTRACTION basis, 1 mg/kg after extraction for lead, cadmium, arsenic and chromium(VI) — a different measured quantity from total content, published separately, with the content instruments enforced alongside as disclosed companions. ONE FASTENER ROW carries the small plated metal components, sampled as their own homogeneous material rather than homogenised into the garment. The toy-migration regime (EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III, three material categories), ASTM F963 soluble elements, EU Regulation 10/2011 specific migration into food, and the EN 1811 nickel-release criterion are all COMPANION OBLIGATIONS recorded on the record and never published as an HMTc content or extraction ceiling. Every subcategory carries a basis_guard that fails the build if a named anchor's register basis leaves the row's declared family. Two open items are recorded rather than papered over: the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 nickel-release restriction is absent from the register and cannot be expressed in its µg/kg unit, so every nickel cell in the category is a control; and the car-seats row is a disclosed read-across because a child restraint system is motor-vehicle equipment outside the US Consumer Product Safety Act definition of a consumer product.

_category.name: Infant and Child Durable Goods and Textiles (Ages 0-5)
_category.anchor: Total-content children's-product and surface-coating law (US CPSIA s.101 and 16 CFR 1303; Canada SOR/2018-83 and SOR/2016-193; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 23; Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 coating values) for durable goods and fasteners, and the EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 extraction limits for clothing, bibs and bedding.
_category.basis_family: Two article bases, declared per row and never conflated. (A) TOTAL CONTENT of the accessible component material — mg/kg of the homogenised component, or of the dried non-volatile film for a coating — which governs the eight durable-goods rows and the fastener row. (B) EXTRACTABLE content of the homogeneous textile material after the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 extraction, which governs the clothing, bib and blanket rows. The leachate and transfer bases — EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48/EC element migration in its three material categories, ASTM F963 soluble elements, EU Regulation 10/2011 specific migration into food, and the EN 1811 nickel-release areal rate — measure different quantities and are recorded as companion conformity obligations, never published as an HMTc ceiling. Each subcategory sets a basis_guard regex that the compiler enforces against every named anchor, so a migration number cannot be published as a content number and a content number cannot be published as an extractable number.
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable maximum set by a credible sovereign government for this exact product form in the row's declared native basis; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign cell where the exact cell is unregulated; a substantiated not-material determination where the analyte is a species bounded by a published parent; and a control with a named reference method where neither a sovereign value nor a supportable read-across exists. Never occurrence-derived.
_category.method_note: Category-specific notes. (1) Species never replace totals: the arsenic values carried by the Australian coating instrument and by REACH Annex XVII entry 72 are unspeciated and are published on tAs, never on iAs; total chromium is reported as a SCREEN because it is dominated by benign Cr(III), with Cr(VI) dispositioned separately. (2) Where the strictest component limit is stricter than another component's own limit, HMTc applies the strictest article-wide — deliberate over-compliance, disclosed in the component set rather than applied silently. (3) Sub-national US statutes that are stricter than the adopted anchors (the Washington Children's Safe Product Act at 40 mg/kg cadmium, Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892 at 75 mg/kg cadmium) are disclosed as jurisdiction-specific companion obligations and logged as register gaps: each statute's own covered-product definition is narrower than the CPSIA children's-product definition, and the register's scope text does not establish whether these product forms are inside the covered list, so applicability to the exact cell cannot be resolved and the value cannot be selected. (4) Nickel is a control on every row in the category because the governing instrument, the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 nickel-release restriction, is expressed as an areal release rate in µg/cm² per week and is not present in the register; EN 1811 testing is required as a companion obligation regardless. (5) Two instruments named in the taxonomy row's regulatory_anchors cannot supply a number under Method v2.0 and are recorded here so their absence is not read as an oversight. OEKO-TEX Standard 100 is a private voluntary certification scheme, not a sovereign instrument, so its extractable-metal values cannot anchor an HMTc cell however strict they are; its extraction philosophy is the same one REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 codifies, and entry 72 is the sovereign instrument this category's textile rows are built on. ASTM F963 is mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106, but its element limits sit in a SOLUBLE (migrated) basis; its lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury and total-chromium values are therefore companion conformity obligations for toy and toy-adjacent components and are excluded from every row's anchor set by the basis guard, notwithstanding that several of them are numerically identical to the content values adopted here. (6) The CPSC durable-infant-or-toddler-product list, also named in the taxonomy row, is a registration and standards-scoping instrument and sets no heavy-metal value; it informs which product forms belong in this category, not what any cell equals.
_category.credible_note: The standing credible-regulator set is widened by one entry for this category: AU (the Commonwealth of Australia), whose Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 carries the only TOTAL-CONTENT arsenic, cadmium and chromium maxima in the register that reach a coated children's article. The existing AU-NZ entry denotes the joint food standards authority and does not cover Australian non-food article law, so the Australian sovereign had to be admitted in its own right for this article category. The addition is scoped to this config and widens the audit scan as well as the anchor set, so any Australian row stricter than a selected binding surfaces as a stricter-unselected warning rather than passing unseen. No sub-national jurisdiction is admitted: US state statutes (US-WA, US-MN, US-CA, US-CT) are disclosed as companion obligations and logged as register gaps for scope-resolved re-ingest.

cribs-and-bassinets.name: Cribs and bassinets
cribs-and-bassinets.native_basis: total element content of each accessible component material of the finished article as placed on market, expressed as mg/kg of the homogenised component (or of the dried non-volatile coating film for a coating component), determined by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS. This is a CONTENT basis. It is not an element-migration or leachate basis (EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48/EC, ASTM F963 soluble elements, EU 10/2011 specific migration into food) and it is not the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 after-extraction textile basis.
cribs-and-bassinets.native_basis_label: total element content of the accessible component material (mg/kg of component; dried non-volatile film for coatings) — a content basis, not a migration or extraction basis
cribs-and-bassinets.scope_note: Full-size and non-full-size cribs, bassinets, cradles, bedside sleepers and their mattress supports, as placed on market. The mattress and any textile sleep surface sold with the unit are sampled as components of this row; loose blankets and sleep sacks route to the blankets-and-sleep-sacks row and are certified on the textile extraction basis. Where the article incorporates a component that is itself a toy — an activity bar, play panel, toy tray, suspended rattle or teether attached to the frame — that component is separately in scope of Directive 2009/48/EC and must meet the EN 71-3 element-migration limits for its own material category (Category I dry/brittle/powder-like/pliable, Category II liquid or sticky, Category III scraped-off; rigid moulded plastic and cured paint on such a component are Category III). Those are 0.07 M HCl leachate limits in a different basis from this row and are recorded as a companion conformity obligation, never as this row's published ceiling.
cribs-and-bassinets.material: solid or engineered hardwood, painted or clear-lacquered wood, powder-coated or plated steel tube, moulded polypropylene and ABS fittings, PVC or polyester teething rail covers, and textile-covered foam mattress
cribs-and-bassinets.components: painted or lacquered wood surface (top rail, slats, end panels); bare wood substrate; powder-coated or plated metal tube; metal fasteners, bolts and mattress-support hardware; moulded plastic fittings, casters and brackets; teething-rail cover; mattress ticking and foam core; applied decals, stickers and printed labels — each sampled and digested as a distinct homogeneous component, with the teething rail, top rail and any surface within the child's mouthing zone sampled first
cribs-and-bassinets.audit_scope: children'?s product|consumer product|accessible part|surface coating|sticker, film|painted article|synthetic organic polymer|toys|childcare|skin contact|leather|furniture|homogeneous material|mouthable|coated with a material
cribs-and-bassinets.basis_guard: ^(?!.*(migration|migratable|soluble|bioavailable|after extraction|leachate|as consumed|as sold|edible|muscle meat|wet weight|product as placed on market|portion ordinarily consumed))(?=.*(content|paint|surface coating|coating material|plastic material|leather|percent by weight|homogeneous material))
cribs-and-bassinets.basis_guard_note: Drawn at the boundary of the TOTAL-CONTENT family. It admits only register rows whose basis is the mass fraction of the element in a homogenised component, coating film, plastic material or metal part, and rejects every leachate/transfer basis: EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48/EC toy migration, ASTM F963 and NOM-252 soluble/bioavailable elements, GB 21027 migratable content, EU 10/2011 specific migration into food, the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 after-extraction textile basis, and all dietary wet-weight and as-consumed food maximum levels. A migration number is a different measured quantity from a content number and must never be published as one; if a named anchor drifts across the boundary the cell resolves to a GAP and the build fails.

Pb.basis_label: total lead content of the accessible component, of the dried coating film and of any applied sticker or film (mg/kg)
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-lead content limit for a children's product and its coatings: 90 mg/kg (US 16 CFR 1303 surface coatings; Canada SOR/2018-83 accessible parts; Canada SOR/2016-193 surface coating materials and applied stickers, films and coatings on furniture and products for children).
Pb.substantiation: Five directly applicable total-content instruments are named and the strictest is taken. The US CPSIA s.101 children's-product substrate limit (100 mg/kg for any part of the product) and the 16 CFR 1303 surface-coating limit (90 mg/kg on the weight of the total non-volatile content of the dried paint film) both reach a crib or bassinet as a children's product; Canada SOR/2018-83 s.2(1) sets 90 mg/kg in each accessible part of consumer products for the sleep, relaxation, hygiene, carrying or transport of children under four; Canada SOR/2016-193 s.2(1) sets 90 mg/kg in a dried sample of surface coating material and s.6 sets 90 mg/kg in stickers, films and applied surface coatings on accessible parts of furniture and products for children. HMTc publishes 90 mg/kg and applies it to every accessible component, including the substrate whose own federal US limit is 100 mg/kg. The EU REACH Annex XVII entry 63 mouthable-article value (500 mg/kg) and the brass-alloy exception (5 000 mg/kg) are far looser and are not selected. A crib is furniture and a product for the sleep of a child under four, so it sits inside both Canadian scopes on their face. Companion sub-national obligations, disclosed and not adopted as the anchor: the Washington Children's Safe Product Act (register rows wa_cspa2008_pb_childrens_products_90ppm, s.3(1)(a), and wa_cspa2008_cd_childrens_products_40ppm, s.3(1)(b)) prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 40 mg/kg in a children's product or product component, and Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892 prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 75 mg/kg in covered consumer products. Both are stricter than the adopted cadmium anchor. Neither is selected here because each statute's own product definition is narrower than the CPSIA 'children's product' definition and the register carries only the phrases 'children's products and product components covered by the Washington Children's Safe Product Act' and 'covered consumer products and product components listed in Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892, subject to exceptions', which do not establish whether this product form is inside the covered list. Applicability to the exact cell cannot be resolved from the register, so the rows are published as jurisdiction-specific companion obligations and logged as register gaps for scope-resolved re-ingest rather than selected as the HMTc value.

components.component: moulded plastic components (fittings, brackets, casters, teething-rail covers and mattress-support hardware)
paint, lacquer and applied surface coatings on coated components
paint on a painted article (EU general cadmium restriction)

component_read_across.basis_label: total cadmium content of the component material (mg/kg of the homogenised component or of the dried coating film)
component_read_across.label: Strictest applicable total-content cadmium limit among this article's principal components: the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 coating value of 75 mg/kg on the non-volatile content of the coating material, read across from coated toys to the coated components of this durable good. HMTc applies the strictest component value article-wide, which is stricter than each component's own limit and never looser.
component_read_across.substantiation: All three candidates are TOTAL-CONTENT limits, so the strictest-of-components selection compares like with like. The EU REACH Annex XVII entry 23 plastic-material value (100 mg/kg) binds the article's moulded polymer components DIRECTLY; the EU painted-article value (1 000 mg/kg) binds its paint layer directly; the Australian coating value (75 mg/kg) is scoped to toys coated with a material and is therefore READ ACROSS to the coatings of a crib or bassinet, which is not a toy but is a coated article for the same child, in the same mouthing and handling contact. Because the read-across value is the strictest of the three it becomes the published ceiling and is applied to every accessible component, including the polymer components whose own direct limit is 100 mg/kg — deliberate over-compliance, disclosed rather than silent. Companion sub-national obligations, disclosed and not adopted as the anchor: the Washington Children's Safe Product Act (register rows wa_cspa2008_pb_childrens_products_90ppm, s.3(1)(a), and wa_cspa2008_cd_childrens_products_40ppm, s.3(1)(b)) prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 40 mg/kg in a children's product or product component, and Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892 prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 75 mg/kg in covered consumer products. Both are stricter than the adopted cadmium anchor. Neither is selected here because each statute's own product definition is narrower than the CPSIA 'children's product' definition and the register carries only the phrases 'children's products and product components covered by the Washington Children's Safe Product Act' and 'covered consumer products and product components listed in Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892, subject to exceptions', which do not establish whether this product form is inside the covered list. Applicability to the exact cell cannot be resolved from the register, so the rows are published as jurisdiction-specific companion obligations and logged as register gaps for scope-resolved re-ingest rather than selected as the HMTc value.

read_across.label: Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 item 2: 25 mg/kg arsenic in the non-volatile content of coating material on a coated toy, read across to the coatings and coated components of this durable good.
read_across.substantiation: This is the only TOTAL-CONTENT arsenic maximum in the register that reaches a coated children's article. It is an unspeciated arsenic value (the register records that arsenic, mercury and chromium are unspecified species in this instrument and are mapped per ingest policy), so it is published on the tAs cell and never on iAs. The read-across is disclosed: the instrument's own scope is 'toys coated with a material' and a crib or bassinet is not a toy, but it is a coated article placed in the same child's hands and mouth, and no credible sovereign sets an arsenic content maximum for the exact cell. The ASTM F963 arsenic value (25 mg/kg) is numerically identical but sits in a soluble-element leachate basis and is excluded by this row's basis guard; the EN 71-3 Category III arsenic migration value (47 mg/kg) is likewise a leachate limit and is looser.

tAs.basis_label: total arsenic content of the coating material and of the accessible component (mg/kg)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes an inorganic-arsenic limit for a crib or bassinet; every arsenic instrument that reaches this category regulates the total element (the Australian coating-content limit adopted for the tAs cell is explicitly an unspeciated arsenic value, and REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 likewise limits arsenic compounds expressed as As metal). Inorganic arsenic is nevertheless NOT declared not-material here, because chromated-copper-arsenate and other arsenical preservative treatment of timber, together with residual arsenical pigments in coatings is a real inorganic-arsenic pathway in this article class and a not-material determination would be an affirmative claim the material contradicts. The species is therefore held under mandatory analytical control, bounded above by the published total-arsenic ceiling.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-arsenic content screen on every accessible component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS (arsenite and arsenate, after a speciation-preserving extraction) on any component returning total arsenic above the reporting limit. Preservative-treated timber, arsenical pigments and recycled-content polymers are sampled as distinct components. Results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule; inorganic arsenic can never exceed the published total-arsenic ceiling by identity.

tHg.basis_label: total mercury content of a dried sample of the surface coating material (mg/kg)
tHg.label: Canada Surface Coating Materials Regulations SOR/2016-193 s.5: not more than 10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried sample of surface coating material.
tHg.substantiation: The instrument's scope in the register is 'surface coating material' with no product qualifier, so it binds the paints, lacquers, primers, printed decals and applied films on a crib or bassinet DIRECTLY rather than by read-across. At 10 mg/kg it is six times stricter than the Australian toy-coating mercury value (60 mg/kg) and matches the Canadian toy-coating mercury limit under SOR/2011-17 s.23(1)(c). HMTc applies it to every accessible component, not only the coating film. The EN 71-3 Category III total-mercury migration value (94 mg/kg) is a leachate limit in another basis and is excluded by this row's basis guard.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a marine-bioaccumulation species. It has no formation route and no established industrial source in a crib or bassinet: the mercury that can occur here comes from pigment, catalyst and preservative residues in coatings, polymers and dyestuffs, all of which are inorganic or aryl-mercury chemistries, and organomercury fungicides in these materials have been withdrawn across every jurisdiction checked. Every sovereign mercury instrument that reaches this article class is written on TOTAL mercury; not one sets a methylmercury value for an article, a coating or a textile. Methylmercury is a proper subset of total mercury by identity, so the published 10 mg/kg total-mercury coating ceiling on this row bounds it absolutely and a separate methylmercury ceiling would add no protection.
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury content screen by microwave-assisted acid digestion with CV-AFS or ICP-MS on every accessible component, with reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS reserved for any component that both exceeds the total-mercury reporting limit and carries a declared organomercury input. No routine methylmercury determination is required.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for an article, a surface coating or a textile. The mercury instruments that reach this category are Canada SOR/2016-193 s.5 (10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried sample of surface coating material), Canada SOR/2011-17 s.23(1)(c) (10 mg/kg total mercury in accessible toy coatings), the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 toy-coating value (60 mg/kg, unspeciated) and Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III (total-mercury migration) — all total-element.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (REACH Annex XVII entries 23, 27, 47, 63, 72; Directive 2009/48/EC; Directive 2011/65/EU RoHS; Regulation 10/2011), US (CPSIA s.101, 16 CFR 1303, ASTM F963 via CPSIA s.106), Canada (SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-82, SOR/2018-83, SOR/2011-17), Australia (Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2), UK, Codex — register-checked, no methylmercury row for any article, coating or textile scope.
not_material.substantiation: Bounded by the total-mercury cell on this same row, which is a published sovereign value in the row's own native basis, so the not-material determination is a speciation bound against a real ceiling rather than an assertion of absence.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a nickel CONTENT maximum for a crib or bassinet. The governing instrument for the actual hazard — allergic contact dermatitis from prolonged skin contact with plated fasteners, mattress-support hardware and exposed metal tube — is the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 nickel-release restriction, which is expressed as an areal release rate (µg/cm² per week) and therefore cannot be expressed in this register's µg/kg content unit; it is not present in the register in any form. The EN 71-3 toy nickel migration values and the EU 10/2011 nickel specific-migration value both sit in leachate bases outside this row's native basis. No number is invented: the cell is held under mandatory analytical control.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-nickel content analysis of every accessible metal, plated and alloy component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, plus EN 1811 nickel-release testing (with EN 12472 wear-and-corrosion pre-treatment for coated or plated parts) on every component in prolonged skin contact, dispositioned against the release criterion in the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 restriction as a companion conformity obligation. That criterion's numeric value is deliberately NOT reproduced here: the restriction is absent from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and this standard quotes no number that is not carried by a named register row. The criterion is applied from the instrument text at audit and is logged as a register gap for ingest through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway. Any component exceeding the release criterion, or any total-nickel result that is an outlier against the supplier's own qualification data, triggers supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a total-tin content maximum for a crib or bassinet. The instrument that does reach this article class — REACH Annex XVII entry 20, which covers textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, childcare articles and other consumer articles in skin contact — restricts ORGANOTIN (dibutyltin and dioctyltin) expressed as tin at 0.1 % by weight. Organotin expressed as tin is a different measurand from total tin: publishing 1 000 mg/kg as this row's total-tin ceiling would pass off a speciated restriction as a total-element limit. The organotin restriction is therefore carried as a companion obligation and no total-tin number is invented. This row DOES read a value across for hexavalent chromium, and the difference is principled rather than convenient: the chromium read-across crosses only a MATERIAL boundary while holding the analyte and the basis fixed, whereas an organotin read-across would cross an ANALYTE boundary, publishing a speciated restriction as a total-element ceiling. A material boundary can be crossed with disclosure; an analyte boundary cannot be crossed at all.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-tin content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with reflex organotin speciation by GC-ICP-MS (dibutyltin, dioctyltin, tributyltin, triphenyltin) on any component returning total tin above the reporting limit. Speciated results are dispositioned against the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 0.1 %-as-tin companion criterion; total-tin results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule against the tightest available supplier qualification context.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes an aluminium content maximum for a crib or bassinet. Aluminium is a structural alloy in this category — frames, tubing, folding mechanisms, rivets and buckle bodies are routinely aluminium by design — so a content ceiling on the homogenised component is not a meaningful contamination control and no sovereign has set one. The EN 71-3 Category III aluminium migration value (28 130 mg/kg) and the EU 10/2011 aluminium specific-migration value (1 mg/kg into food) are leachate limits in other bases and are not read across into a content ceiling. No number is invented.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-aluminium content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on every non-structural accessible component (coatings, plastics, textiles, foams, printed decals), with structural aluminium alloy components identified and dispositioned by declared alloy specification rather than by a contamination ceiling. Aluminium detected in a component whose declared composition contains no aluminium is treated as a contamination signal and escalated to supplier corrective action.

read_across.label: Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 item 2: 60 mg/kg chromium in the non-volatile content of coating material on a coated toy, read across to the coatings and coated components of this durable good. Reported as a SCREEN.
read_across.substantiation: The instrument records chromium as an unspecified species and the register maps it to total chromium. Total chromium in these materials is dominated by benign trivalent chromium — chrome-tanned leather trim, chromium(III) oxide pigments, stainless-steel alloy — so the value is recorded as a screen and is not treated as a standalone protective ceiling. The health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which is dispositioned on this row's Cr-VI control with the REACH Annex XVII entry 47 leather limit as a binding companion. The ASTM F963 total-chromium value (60 mg/kg) is numerically identical but sits in a soluble-element leachate basis and is excluded by this row's basis guard.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is a screen cell, not a firm protective ceiling: the measured total is dominated by trivalent chromium from tanning agents, chromium(III) pigments and stainless-steel alloy, while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). A total-chromium result at or below 60 mg/kg does not by itself demonstrate Cr(VI) compliance, and a total-chromium detection is the trigger for the Cr(VI) determination on this same row.
Cr.basis_label: total chromium content of the coating material and of the accessible component (mg/kg)

read_across.label: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 47 paragraphs 5 and 6 (Regulation (EU) No 301/2014): 3 mg/kg hexavalent chromium on the total dry weight of leather, for leather articles and articles containing leather parts coming into contact with the skin. Applied article-wide.
read_across.substantiation: This is the only hexavalent-chromium CONTENT limit in the register that reaches a skin-contact article, and it binds DIRECTLY wherever a crib or bassinet carries a leather part in skin contact — a leather handlebar or bumper-bar wrap, a harness pad, a leather trim panel or a leather pull tab. For the article's non-leather Cr(VI) pathways — chromate-pigmented coatings, chromate conversion coatings and hexavalent chrome plating on metal parts — no sovereign sets a content maximum, so the 3 mg/kg value is READ ACROSS to them and applied article-wide. The read-across is disclosed and is argued from the material and the contact, not from convenience: it keeps the SAME analyte (Cr(VI) specifically, not total chromium) and the SAME basis (mg/kg of the component's dry mass), and crosses only a material boundary, from chrome-tanned leather to a chromate-pigmented or chromate-passivated surface. The hazard is identical (Cr(VI) skin sensitisation) and the route is identical (dermal transfer under sweat from a surface held against the child), which is exactly why entry 47 was written for skin-contact leather in the first place. Applying it article-wide is deliberate over-compliance and is the same rule this row applies to lead (90 mg/kg applied to a substrate whose own US limit is 100 mg/kg) and to cadmium (75 mg/kg applied to polymer components whose own EU limit is 100 mg/kg); declining to extend it to Cr(VI), the analyte where compliance costs a supplier a change of passivation chemistry, would be selective over-compliance and is not done. The EU RoHS 0.1 % homogeneous-material Cr(VI) value is scoped to electrical and electronic equipment and is over three hundred times more permissive, so it is not used as the read-across source. The EN 71-3 Category I and II Cr(VI) migration values are numerically lower but are leachate limits measuring transfer rather than content, and are excluded by this row's basis guard.

Cr-VI.basis_label: hexavalent chromium content on the total dry weight of the component (mg/kg) — leather, coating film, or plated and conversion-coated metal part
Cr-VI.binding_control: Determined by ISO 17075-1/-2 on every leather and leather-containing component, and by alkaline digestion with ion chromatography and post-column derivatisation (US EPA 3060A / 7199 approach) on chromate-pigmented coatings, chromate conversion coatings and plated metal parts. A leather component above the published value is a direct breach of REACH Annex XVII entry 47; a non-leather component above it breaches the read-across ceiling and triggers supplier corrective action and substitution to trivalent-chromium or chromium-free passivation.

play-yards-and-gates.name: Play yards and gates/enclosures
play-yards-and-gates.native_basis: total element content of each accessible component material of the finished article as placed on market, expressed as mg/kg of the homogenised component (or of the dried non-volatile coating film for a coating component), determined by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS. This is a CONTENT basis. It is not an element-migration or leachate basis (EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48/EC, ASTM F963 soluble elements, EU 10/2011 specific migration into food) and it is not the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 after-extraction textile basis.
play-yards-and-gates.native_basis_label: total element content of the accessible component material (mg/kg of component; dried non-volatile film for coatings) — a content basis, not a migration or extraction basis
play-yards-and-gates.scope_note: Play yards, playpens, portable cribs sold as play yards, pressure- and hardware-mounted safety gates, and free-standing play enclosures. Activity panels, suspended toys and toy bars supplied with the unit are components of this row for content testing and are additionally toys in their own right under Directive 2009/48/EC. Pb.basis_label: total lead content of the accessible component, of the dried coating film and of any applied sticker or film (mg/kg)
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-lead content limit for a children's product and its coatings: 90 mg/kg (US 16 CFR 1303 surface coatings; Canada SOR/2018-83 accessible parts; Canada SOR/2016-193 surface coating materials and applied stickers, films and coatings on furniture and products for children).
Pb.substantiation: Five directly applicable total-content instruments are named and the strictest is taken. The US CPSIA s.101 children's-product substrate limit (100 mg/kg for any part of the product) and the 16 CFR 1303 surface-coating limit (90 mg/kg on the weight of the total non-volatile content of the dried paint film) both reach a play yard, gate or play enclosure as a children's product; Canada SOR/2018-83 s.2(1) sets 90 mg/kg in each accessible part of consumer products for the sleep, relaxation, hygiene, carrying or transport of children under four; Canada SOR/2016-193 s.2(1) sets 90 mg/kg in a dried sample of surface coating material and s.6 sets 90 mg/kg in stickers, films and applied surface coatings on accessible parts of furniture and products for children. HMTc publishes 90 mg/kg and applies it to every accessible component, including the substrate whose own federal US limit is 100 mg/kg. The EU REACH Annex XVII entry 63 mouthable-article value (500 mg/kg) and the brass-alloy exception (5 000 mg/kg) are far looser and are not selected. A play yard and a safety gate are children's products under CPSIA and are products for the relaxation and play of a child under four under SOR/2018-83. Companion sub-national obligations, disclosed and not adopted as the anchor: the Washington Children's Safe Product Act (register rows wa_cspa2008_pb_childrens_products_90ppm, s.3(1)(a), and wa_cspa2008_cd_childrens_products_40ppm, s.3(1)(b)) prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 40 mg/kg in a children's product or product component, and Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892 prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 75 mg/kg in covered consumer products. Both are stricter than the adopted cadmium anchor. Neither is selected here because each statute's own product definition is narrower than the CPSIA 'children's product' definition and the register carries only the phrases 'children's products and product components covered by the Washington Children's Safe Product Act' and 'covered consumer products and product components listed in Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892, subject to exceptions', which do not establish whether this product form is inside the covered list. Applicability to the exact cell cannot be resolved from the register, so the rows are published as jurisdiction-specific companion obligations and logged as register gaps for scope-resolved re-ingest rather than selected as the HMTc value.

read_across.label: Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 item 2: 25 mg/kg arsenic in the non-volatile content of coating material on a coated toy, read across to the coatings and coated components of this durable good.
read_across.substantiation: This is the only TOTAL-CONTENT arsenic maximum in the register that reaches a coated children's article. It is an unspeciated arsenic value (the register records that arsenic, mercury and chromium are unspecified species in this instrument and are mapped per ingest policy), so it is published on the tAs cell and never on iAs. The read-across is disclosed: the instrument's own scope is 'toys coated with a material' and a play yard, playpen, safety gate or play enclosure is not a toy, but it is a coated article placed in the same child's hands and mouth, and no credible sovereign sets an arsenic content maximum for the exact cell. The ASTM F963 arsenic value (25 mg/kg) is numerically identical but sits in a soluble-element leachate basis and is excluded by this row's basis guard; the EN 71-3 Category III arsenic migration value (47 mg/kg) is likewise a leachate limit and is looser.

tAs.basis_label: total arsenic content of the coating material and of the accessible component (mg/kg)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes an inorganic-arsenic limit for a play yard, playpen, safety gate or play enclosure; every arsenic instrument that reaches this category regulates the total element (the Australian coating-content limit adopted for the tAs cell is explicitly an unspeciated arsenic value, and REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 likewise limits arsenic compounds expressed as As metal). Inorganic arsenic is nevertheless NOT declared not-material here, because residual arsenical pigments in coatings and printed decals, and arsenic carried in recycled-content polymer feedstock is a real inorganic-arsenic pathway in this article class and a not-material determination would be an affirmative claim the material contradicts. The species is therefore held under mandatory analytical control, bounded above by the published total-arsenic ceiling.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-arsenic content screen on every accessible component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS (arsenite and arsenate, after a speciation-preserving extraction) on any component returning total arsenic above the reporting limit. Preservative-treated timber, arsenical pigments and recycled-content polymers are sampled as distinct components. Results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule; inorganic arsenic can never exceed the published total-arsenic ceiling by identity.

tHg.basis_label: total mercury content of a dried sample of the surface coating material (mg/kg)
tHg.label: Canada Surface Coating Materials Regulations SOR/2016-193 s.5: not more than 10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried sample of surface coating material.
tHg.substantiation: The instrument's scope in the register is 'surface coating material' with no product qualifier, so it binds the paints, lacquers, primers, printed decals and applied films on a play yard, playpen, safety gate or play enclosure DIRECTLY rather than by read-across. At 10 mg/kg it is six times stricter than the Australian toy-coating mercury value (60 mg/kg) and matches the Canadian toy-coating mercury limit under SOR/2011-17 s.23(1)(c). HMTc applies it to every accessible component, not only the coating film. The EN 71-3 Category III total-mercury migration value (94 mg/kg) is a leachate limit in another basis and is excluded by this row's basis guard.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a marine-bioaccumulation species. It has no formation route and no established industrial source in a play yard, playpen, safety gate or play enclosure: the mercury that can occur here comes from pigment, catalyst and preservative residues in coatings, polymers and dyestuffs, all of which are inorganic or aryl-mercury chemistries, and organomercury fungicides in these materials have been withdrawn across every jurisdiction checked. Every sovereign mercury instrument that reaches this article class is written on TOTAL mercury; not one sets a methylmercury value for an article, a coating or a textile. Methylmercury is a proper subset of total mercury by identity, so the published 10 mg/kg total-mercury coating ceiling on this row bounds it absolutely and a separate methylmercury ceiling would add no protection.
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury content screen by microwave-assisted acid digestion with CV-AFS or ICP-MS on every accessible component, with reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS reserved for any component that both exceeds the total-mercury reporting limit and carries a declared organomercury input. No routine methylmercury determination is required.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for an article, a surface coating or a textile. The mercury instruments that reach this category are Canada SOR/2016-193 s.5 (10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried sample of surface coating material), Canada SOR/2011-17 s.23(1)(c) (10 mg/kg total mercury in accessible toy coatings), the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 toy-coating value (60 mg/kg, unspeciated) and Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III (total-mercury migration) — all total-element.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (REACH Annex XVII entries 23, 27, 47, 63, 72; Directive 2009/48/EC; Directive 2011/65/EU RoHS; Regulation 10/2011), US (CPSIA s.101, 16 CFR 1303, ASTM F963 via CPSIA s.106), Canada (SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-82, SOR/2018-83, SOR/2011-17), Australia (Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2), UK, Codex — register-checked, no methylmercury row for any article, coating or textile scope.
not_material.substantiation: Bounded by the total-mercury cell on this same row, which is a published sovereign value in the row's own native basis, so the not-material determination is a speciation bound against a real ceiling rather than an assertion of absence.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a nickel CONTENT maximum for a play yard, playpen, safety gate or play enclosure. The governing instrument for the actual hazard — allergic contact dermatitis from prolonged skin contact with plated latches, hinge pins, locking hardware and exposed metal tube — is the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 nickel-release restriction, which is expressed as an areal release rate (µg/cm² per week) and therefore cannot be expressed in this register's µg/kg content unit; it is not present in the register in any form. The EN 71-3 toy nickel migration values and the EU 10/2011 nickel specific-migration value both sit in leachate bases outside this row's native basis. No number is invented: the cell is held under mandatory analytical control.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-nickel content analysis of every accessible metal, plated and alloy component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, plus EN 1811 nickel-release testing (with EN 12472 wear-and-corrosion pre-treatment for coated or plated parts) on every component in prolonged skin contact, dispositioned against the release criterion in the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 restriction as a companion conformity obligation. That criterion's numeric value is deliberately NOT reproduced here: the restriction is absent from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and this standard quotes no number that is not carried by a named register row. The criterion is applied from the instrument text at audit and is logged as a register gap for ingest through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway. Any component exceeding the release criterion, or any total-nickel result that is an outlier against the supplier's own qualification data, triggers supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a total-tin content maximum for a play yard, playpen, safety gate or play enclosure. The instrument that does reach this article class — REACH Annex XVII entry 20, which covers textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, childcare articles and other consumer articles in skin contact — restricts ORGANOTIN (dibutyltin and dioctyltin) expressed as tin at 0.1 % by weight. Organotin expressed as tin is a different measurand from total tin: publishing 1 000 mg/kg as this row's total-tin ceiling would pass off a speciated restriction as a total-element limit. The organotin restriction is therefore carried as a companion obligation and no total-tin number is invented. This row DOES read a value across for hexavalent chromium, and the difference is principled rather than convenient: the chromium read-across crosses only a MATERIAL boundary while holding the analyte and the basis fixed, whereas an organotin read-across would cross an ANALYTE boundary, publishing a speciated restriction as a total-element ceiling. A material boundary can be crossed with disclosure; an analyte boundary cannot be crossed at all.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-tin content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with reflex organotin speciation by GC-ICP-MS (dibutyltin, dioctyltin, tributyltin, triphenyltin) on any component returning total tin above the reporting limit. Speciated results are dispositioned against the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 0.1 %-as-tin companion criterion; total-tin results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule against the tightest available supplier qualification context.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes an aluminium content maximum for a play yard, playpen, safety gate or play enclosure. Aluminium is a structural alloy in this category — frames, tubing, folding mechanisms, rivets and buckle bodies are routinely aluminium by design — so a content ceiling on the homogenised component is not a meaningful contamination control and no sovereign has set one. The EN 71-3 Category III aluminium migration value (28 130 mg/kg) and the EU 10/2011 aluminium specific-migration value (1 mg/kg into food) are leachate limits in other bases and are not read across into a content ceiling. No number is invented.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-aluminium content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on every non-structural accessible component (coatings, plastics, textiles, foams, printed decals), with structural aluminium alloy components identified and dispositioned by declared alloy specification rather than by a contamination ceiling. Aluminium detected in a component whose declared composition contains no aluminium is treated as a contamination signal and escalated to supplier corrective action.

read_across.label: Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 item 2: 60 mg/kg chromium in the non-volatile content of coating material on a coated toy, read across to the coatings and coated components of this durable good. Reported as a SCREEN.
read_across.substantiation: The instrument records chromium as an unspecified species and the register maps it to total chromium. Total chromium in these materials is dominated by benign trivalent chromium — chrome-tanned leather trim, chromium(III) oxide pigments, stainless-steel alloy — so the value is recorded as a screen and is not treated as a standalone protective ceiling. The health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which is dispositioned on this row's Cr-VI control with the REACH Annex XVII entry 47 leather limit as a binding companion. The ASTM F963 total-chromium value (60 mg/kg) is numerically identical but sits in a soluble-element leachate basis and is excluded by this row's basis guard.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is a screen cell, not a firm protective ceiling: the measured total is dominated by trivalent chromium from tanning agents, chromium(III) pigments and stainless-steel alloy, while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). A total-chromium result at or below 60 mg/kg does not by itself demonstrate Cr(VI) compliance, and a total-chromium detection is the trigger for the Cr(VI) determination on this same row.
Cr.basis_label: total chromium content of the coating material and of the accessible component (mg/kg)

read_across.label: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 47 paragraphs 5 and 6 (Regulation (EU) No 301/2014): 3 mg/kg hexavalent chromium on the total dry weight of leather, for leather articles and articles containing leather parts coming into contact with the skin. Applied article-wide.
read_across.substantiation: This is the only hexavalent-chromium CONTENT limit in the register that reaches a skin-contact article, and it binds DIRECTLY wherever a play yard, playpen, safety gate or play enclosure carries a leather part in skin contact — a leather handlebar or bumper-bar wrap, a harness pad, a leather trim panel or a leather pull tab. For the article's non-leather Cr(VI) pathways — chromate-pigmented coatings, chromate conversion coatings and hexavalent chrome plating on metal parts — no sovereign sets a content maximum, so the 3 mg/kg value is READ ACROSS to them and applied article-wide. The read-across is disclosed and is argued from the material and the contact, not from convenience: it keeps the SAME analyte (Cr(VI) specifically, not total chromium) and the SAME basis (mg/kg of the component's dry mass), and crosses only a material boundary, from chrome-tanned leather to a chromate-pigmented or chromate-passivated surface. The hazard is identical (Cr(VI) skin sensitisation) and the route is identical (dermal transfer under sweat from a surface held against the child), which is exactly why entry 47 was written for skin-contact leather in the first place. Applying it article-wide is deliberate over-compliance and is the same rule this row applies to lead (90 mg/kg applied to a substrate whose own US limit is 100 mg/kg) and to cadmium (75 mg/kg applied to polymer components whose own EU limit is 100 mg/kg); declining to extend it to Cr(VI), the analyte where compliance costs a supplier a change of passivation chemistry, would be selective over-compliance and is not done. The EU RoHS 0.1 % homogeneous-material Cr(VI) value is scoped to electrical and electronic equipment and is over three hundred times more permissive, so it is not used as the read-across source. The EN 71-3 Category I and II Cr(VI) migration values are numerically lower but are leachate limits measuring transfer rather than content, and are excluded by this row's basis guard.

Cr-VI.basis_label: hexavalent chromium content on the total dry weight of the component (mg/kg) — leather, coating film, or plated and conversion-coated metal part
Cr-VI.binding_control: Determined by ISO 17075-1/-2 on every leather and leather-containing component, and by alkaline digestion with ion chromatography and post-column derivatisation (US EPA 3060A / 7199 approach) on chromate-pigmented coatings, chromate conversion coatings and plated metal parts. A leather component above the published value is a direct breach of REACH Annex XVII entry 47; a non-leather component above it breaches the read-across ceiling and triggers supplier corrective action and substitution to trivalent-chromium or chromium-free passivation.

It is an unspeciated arsenic value (the register records that arsenic, mercury and chromium are unspecified species in this instrument and are mapped per ingest policy), so it is published on the tAs cell and never on iAs. The read-across is disclosed: the instrument's own scope is 'toys coated with a material' and a stroller or pram is not a toy, but it is a coated article placed in the same child's hands and mouth, and no credible sovereign sets an arsenic content maximum for the exact cell. The ASTM F963 arsenic value (25 mg/kg) is numerically identical but sits in a soluble-element leachate basis and is excluded by this row's basis guard; the EN 71-3 Category III arsenic migration value (47 mg/kg) is likewise a leachate limit and is looser.

tAs.basis_label: total arsenic content of the coating material and of the accessible component (mg/kg)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes an inorganic-arsenic limit for a stroller or pram; every arsenic instrument that reaches this category regulates the total element (the Australian coating-content limit adopted for the tAs cell is explicitly an unspeciated arsenic value, and REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 likewise limits arsenic compounds expressed as As metal). Inorganic arsenic is nevertheless NOT declared not-material here, because residual arsenical pigments in coatings and printed fabric, and arsenic carried in recycled-content polymer and rubber feedstock is a real inorganic-arsenic pathway in this article class and a not-material determination would be an affirmative claim the material contradicts. The species is therefore held under mandatory analytical control, bounded above by the published total-arsenic ceiling.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-arsenic content screen on every accessible component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS (arsenite and arsenate, after a speciation-preserving extraction) on any component returning total arsenic above the reporting limit. Preservative-treated timber, arsenical pigments and recycled-content polymers are sampled as distinct components. Results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule; inorganic arsenic can never exceed the published total-arsenic ceiling by identity.

tHg.basis_label: total mercury content of a dried sample of the surface coating material (mg/kg)
tHg.label: Canada Surface Coating Materials Regulations SOR/2016-193 s.5: not more than 10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried sample of surface coating material.
tHg.substantiation: The instrument's scope in the register is 'surface coating material' with no product qualifier, so it binds the paints, lacquers, primers, printed decals and applied films on a stroller or pram DIRECTLY rather than by read-across. At 10 mg/kg it is six times stricter than the Australian toy-coating mercury value (60 mg/kg) and matches the Canadian toy-coating mercury limit under SOR/2011-17 s.23(1)(c). HMTc applies it to every accessible component, not only the coating film. The EN 71-3 Category III total-mercury migration value (94 mg/kg) is a leachate limit in another basis and is excluded by this row's basis guard.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a marine-bioaccumulation species. It has no formation route and no established industrial source in a stroller or pram: the mercury that can occur here comes from pigment, catalyst and preservative residues in coatings, polymers and dyestuffs, all of which are inorganic or aryl-mercury chemistries, and organomercury fungicides in these materials have been withdrawn across every jurisdiction checked. Every sovereign mercury instrument that reaches this article class is written on TOTAL mercury; not one sets a methylmercury value for an article, a coating or a textile. Methylmercury is a proper subset of total mercury by identity, so the published 10 mg/kg total-mercury coating ceiling on this row bounds it absolutely and a separate methylmercury ceiling would add no protection.
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury content screen by microwave-assisted acid digestion with CV-AFS or ICP-MS on every accessible component, with reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS reserved for any component that both exceeds the total-mercury reporting limit and carries a declared organomercury input. No routine methylmercury determination is required.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for an article, a surface coating or a textile. The mercury instruments that reach this category are Canada SOR/2016-193 s.5 (10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried sample of surface coating material), Canada SOR/2011-17 s.23(1)(c) (10 mg/kg total mercury in accessible toy coatings), the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 toy-coating value (60 mg/kg, unspeciated) and Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III (total-mercury migration) — all total-element.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (REACH Annex XVII entries 23, 27, 47, 63, 72; Directive 2009/48/EC; Directive 2011/65/EU RoHS; Regulation 10/2011), US (CPSIA s.101, 16 CFR 1303, ASTM F963 via CPSIA s.106), Canada (SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-82, SOR/2018-83, SOR/2011-17), Australia (Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2), UK, Codex — register-checked, no methylmercury row for any article, coating or textile scope.
not_material.substantiation: Bounded by the total-mercury cell on this same row, which is a published sovereign value in the row's own native basis, so the not-material determination is a speciation bound against a real ceiling rather than an assertion of absence.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a nickel CONTENT maximum for a stroller or pram. The governing instrument for the actual hazard — allergic contact dermatitis from prolonged skin contact with harness buckles, frame-lock pins, plated fasteners and exposed metal tube — is the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 nickel-release restriction, which is expressed as an areal release rate (µg/cm² per week) and therefore cannot be expressed in this register's µg/kg content unit; it is not present in the register in any form. The EN 71-3 toy nickel migration values and the EU 10/2011 nickel specific-migration value both sit in leachate bases outside this row's native basis. No number is invented: the cell is held under mandatory analytical control.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-nickel content analysis of every accessible metal, plated and alloy component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, plus EN 1811 nickel-release testing (with EN 12472 wear-and-corrosion pre-treatment for coated or plated parts) on every component in prolonged skin contact, dispositioned against the release criterion in the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 restriction as a companion conformity obligation. That criterion's numeric value is deliberately NOT reproduced here: the restriction is absent from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and this standard quotes no number that is not carried by a named register row. The criterion is applied from the instrument text at audit and is logged as a register gap for ingest through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway. Any component exceeding the release criterion, or any total-nickel result that is an outlier against the supplier's own qualification data, triggers supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a total-tin content maximum for a stroller or pram. The instrument that does reach this article class — REACH Annex XVII entry 20, which covers textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, childcare articles and other consumer articles in skin contact — restricts ORGANOTIN (dibutyltin and dioctyltin) expressed as tin at 0.1 % by weight. Organotin expressed as tin is a different measurand from total tin: publishing 1 000 mg/kg as this row's total-tin ceiling would pass off a speciated restriction as a total-element limit. The organotin restriction is therefore carried as a companion obligation and no total-tin number is invented. This row DOES read a value across for hexavalent chromium, and the difference is principled rather than convenient: the chromium read-across crosses only a MATERIAL boundary while holding the analyte and the basis fixed, whereas an organotin read-across would cross an ANALYTE boundary, publishing a speciated restriction as a total-element ceiling. A material boundary can be crossed with disclosure; an analyte boundary cannot be crossed at all.

Speciated results are dispositioned against the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 0.1 %-as-tin companion criterion; total-tin results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule against the tightest available supplier qualification context.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes an aluminium content maximum for a stroller or pram. The EN 71-3 Category III aluminium migration value (28 130 mg/kg) and the EU 10/2011 aluminium specific-migration value (1 mg/kg into food) are leachate limits in other bases and are not read across into a content ceiling. No number is invented.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-aluminium content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on every non-structural accessible component (coatings, plastics, textiles, foams, printed decals), with structural aluminium alloy components identified and dispositioned by declared alloy specification rather than by a contamination ceiling. Aluminium detected in a component whose declared composition contains no aluminium is treated as a contamination signal and escalated to supplier corrective action.

read_across.label: Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 item 2: 60 mg/kg chromium in the non-volatile content of coating material on a coated toy, read across to the coatings and coated components of this durable good. Reported as a SCREEN.
read_across.substantiation: The instrument records chromium as an unspecified species and the register maps it to total chromium. Total chromium in these materials is dominated by benign trivalent chromium — chrome-tanned leather trim, chromium(III) oxide pigments, stainless-steel alloy — so the value is recorded as a screen and is not treated as a standalone protective ceiling. The health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which is dispositioned on this row's Cr-VI control with the REACH Annex XVII entry 47 leather limit as a binding companion. The ASTM F963 total-chromium value (60 mg/kg) is numerically identical but sits in a soluble-element leachate basis and is excluded by this row's basis guard.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is a screen cell, not a firm protective ceiling: the measured total is dominated by trivalent chromium from tanning agents, chromium(III) pigments and stainless-steel alloy, while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). A total-chromium result at or below 60 mg/kg does not by itself demonstrate Cr(VI) compliance, and a total-chromium detection is the trigger for the Cr(VI) determination on this same row.
Cr.basis_label: total chromium content of the coating material and of the accessible component (mg/kg)

read_across.label: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 47 paragraphs 5 and 6 (Regulation (EU) No 301/2014): 3 mg/kg hexavalent chromium on the total dry weight of leather, for leather articles and articles containing leather parts coming into contact with the skin. Applied article-wide.
read_across.substantiation: This is the only hexavalent-chromium CONTENT limit in the register that reaches a skin-contact article, and it binds DIRECTLY wherever a stroller or pram carries a leather part in skin contact — a leather handlebar or bumper-bar wrap, a harness pad, a leather trim panel or a leather pull tab. For the article's non-leather Cr(VI) pathways — chromate-pigmented coatings, chromate conversion coatings and hexavalent chrome plating on metal parts — no sovereign sets a content maximum, so the 3 mg/kg value is READ ACROSS to them and applied article-wide. The read-across is disclosed and is argued from the material and the contact, not from convenience: it keeps the SAME analyte (Cr(VI) specifically, not total chromium) and the SAME basis (mg/kg of the component's dry mass), and crosses only a material boundary, from chrome-tanned leather to a chromate-pigmented or chromate-passivated surface. The hazard is identical (Cr(VI) skin sensitisation) and the route is identical (dermal transfer under sweat from a surface held against the child), which is exactly why entry 47 was written for skin-contact leather in the first place. Applying it article-wide is deliberate over-compliance and is the same rule this row applies to lead (90 mg/kg applied to a substrate whose own US limit is 100 mg/kg) and to cadmium (75 mg/kg applied to polymer components whose own EU limit is 100 mg/kg); declining to extend it to Cr(VI), the analyte where compliance costs a supplier a change of passivation chemistry, would be selective over-compliance and is not done. The EU RoHS 0.1 % homogeneous-material Cr(VI) value is scoped to electrical and electronic equipment and is over three hundred times more permissive, so it is not used as the read-across source. The EN 71-3 Category I and II Cr(VI) migration values are numerically lower but are leachate limits measuring transfer rather than content, and are excluded by this row's basis guard.

Cr-VI.basis_label: hexavalent chromium content on the total dry weight of the component (mg/kg) — leather, coating film, or plated and conversion-coated metal part
Cr-VI.binding_control: Determined by ISO 17075-1/-2 on every leather and leather-containing component, and by alkaline digestion with ion chromatography and post-column derivatisation (US EPA 3060A / 7199 approach) on chromate-pigmented coatings, chromate conversion coatings and plated metal parts. A leather component above the published value is a direct breach of REACH Annex XVII entry 47; a non-leather component above it breaches the read-across ceiling and triggers supplier corrective action and substitution to trivalent-chromium or chromium-free passivation.

walkers.name: Walkers
walkers.native_basis: total element content of each accessible component material of the finished article as placed on market, expressed as mg/kg of the homogenised component (or of the dried non-volatile coating film for a coating component), determined by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS. This is a CONTENT basis. It is not an element-migration or leachate basis (EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48/EC, ASTM F963 soluble elements, EU 10/2011 specific migration into food) and it is not the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 after-extraction textile basis.
walkers.native_basis_label: total element content of the accessible component material (mg/kg of component; dried non-volatile film for coatings) — a content basis, not a migration or extraction basis
walkers.scope_note: Seated infant walkers, sit-to-stand and push walkers, and activity walkers with a play tray. The play tray, its toys and its printed graphics are components of this row for content testing and are additionally toys under Directive 2009/48/EC. Where the article incorporates a component that is itself a toy — an activity bar, play panel, toy tray, suspended rattle or teether attached to the frame — that component is separately in scope of Directive 2009/48/EC and must meet the EN 71-3 element-migration limits for its own material category (Category I dry/brittle/powder-like/pliable, Category II liquid or sticky, Category III scraped-off; rigid moulded plastic and cured paint on such a component are Category III). walkers.material: moulded polypropylene and ABS base, tray and frame, powder-coated or plated steel tube, polyester seat sling with foam padding, PVC or TPE toy elements, and printed tray graphics
walkers.components: moulded plastic base, frame and tray; printed tray graphic and applied decal; powder-coated or plated metal tube; seat-sling fabric, foam and its binding; plastic and elastomer toy elements on the tray; casters and metal fasteners — each sampled and digested as a distinct homogeneous component, with the tray surface, tray graphic and any detachable toy element sampled first

walkers.basis_guard_note: Drawn at the boundary of the TOTAL-CONTENT family. It admits only register rows whose basis is the mass fraction of the element in a homogenised component, coating film, plastic material or metal part, and rejects every leachate/transfer basis: EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48/EC toy migration, ASTM F963 and NOM-252 soluble/bioavailable elements, GB 21027 migratable content, EU 10/2011 specific migration into food, the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 after-extraction textile basis, and all dietary wet-weight and as-consumed food maximum levels. A migration number is a different measured quantity from a content number and must never be published as one; if a named anchor drifts across the boundary the cell resolves to a GAP and the build fails.

Pb.basis_label: total lead content of the accessible component, of the dried coating film and of any applied sticker or film (mg/kg)
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-lead content limit for a children's product and its coatings: 90 mg/kg (US 16 CFR 1303 surface coatings; Canada SOR/2018-83 accessible parts; Canada SOR/2016-193 surface coating materials and applied stickers, films and coatings on furniture and products for children).
Pb.substantiation: Five directly applicable total-content instruments are named and the strictest is taken. The US CPSIA s.101 children's-product substrate limit (100 mg/kg for any part of the product) and the 16 CFR 1303 surface-coating limit (90 mg/kg on the weight of the total non-volatile content of the dried paint film) both reach a walker as a children's product; Canada SOR/2018-83 s.2(1) sets 90 mg/kg in each accessible part of consumer products for the sleep, relaxation, hygiene, carrying or transport of children under four; Canada SOR/2016-193 s.2(1) sets 90 mg/kg in a dried sample of surface coating material and s.6 sets 90 mg/kg in stickers, films and applied surface coatings on accessible parts of furniture and products for children. HMTc publishes 90 mg/kg and applies it to every accessible component, including the substrate whose own federal US limit is 100 mg/kg. The EU REACH Annex XVII entry 63 mouthable-article value (500 mg/kg) and the brass-alloy exception (5 000 mg/kg) are far looser and are not selected. A walker is a children's product under CPSIA and a child learning and play product under SOR/2018-83. Companion sub-national obligations, disclosed and not adopted as the anchor: the Washington Children's Safe Product Act (register rows wa_cspa2008_pb_childrens_products_90ppm, s.3(1)(a), and wa_cspa2008_cd_childrens_products_40ppm, s.3(1)(b)) prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 40 mg/kg in a children's product or product component, and Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892 prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 75 mg/kg in covered consumer products. Both are stricter than the adopted cadmium anchor. Neither is selected here because each statute's own product definition is narrower than the CPSIA 'children's product' definition and the register carries only the phrases 'children's products and product components covered by the Washington Children's Safe Product Act' and 'covered consumer products and product components listed in Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892, subject to exceptions', which do not establish whether this product form is inside the covered list. Applicability to the exact cell cannot be resolved from the register, so the rows are published as jurisdiction-specific companion obligations and logged as register gaps for scope-resolved re-ingest rather than selected as the HMTc value.

component_read_across.basis_label: total cadmium content of the component material (mg/kg of the homogenised component or of the dried coating film)
component_read_across.label: Strictest applicable total-content cadmium limit among this article's principal components: the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 coating value of 75 mg/kg on the non-volatile content of the coating material, read across from coated toys to the coated components of this durable good. The EN 71-3 Category III aluminium migration value (28 130 mg/kg) and the EU 10/2011 aluminium specific-migration value (1 mg/kg into food) are leachate limits in other bases and are not read across into a content ceiling. No number is invented.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-aluminium content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on every non-structural accessible component (coatings, plastics, textiles, foams, printed decals), with structural aluminium alloy components identified and dispositioned by declared alloy specification rather than by a contamination ceiling. Aluminium detected in a component whose declared composition contains no aluminium is treated as a contamination signal and escalated to supplier corrective action.

read_across.label: Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 item 2: 60 mg/kg chromium in the non-volatile content of coating material on a coated toy, read across to the coatings and coated components of this durable good. Reported as a SCREEN.
read_across.substantiation: The instrument records chromium as an unspecified species and the register maps it to total chromium. Total chromium in these materials is dominated by benign trivalent chromium — chrome-tanned leather trim, chromium(III) oxide pigments, stainless-steel alloy — so the value is recorded as a screen and is not treated as a standalone protective ceiling. The health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which is dispositioned on this row's Cr-VI control with the REACH Annex XVII entry 47 leather limit as a binding companion. The ASTM F963 total-chromium value (60 mg/kg) is numerically identical but sits in a soluble-element leachate basis and is excluded by this row's basis guard.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is a screen cell, not a firm protective ceiling: the measured total is dominated by trivalent chromium from tanning agents, chromium(III) pigments and stainless-steel alloy, while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). A total-chromium result at or below 60 mg/kg does not by itself demonstrate Cr(VI) compliance, and a total-chromium detection is the trigger for the Cr(VI) determination on this same row.
Cr.basis_label: total chromium content of the coating material and of the accessible component (mg/kg)

read_across.label: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 47 paragraphs 5 and 6 (Regulation (EU) No 301/2014): 3 mg/kg hexavalent chromium on the total dry weight of leather, for leather articles and articles containing leather parts coming into contact with the skin. Applied article-wide.
read_across.substantiation: This is the only hexavalent-chromium CONTENT limit in the register that reaches a skin-contact article, and it binds DIRECTLY wherever an infant walker or activity walker carries a leather part in skin contact — a leather handlebar or bumper-bar wrap, a harness pad, a leather trim panel or a leather pull tab. For the article's non-leather Cr(VI) pathways — chromate-pigmented coatings, chromate conversion coatings and hexavalent chrome plating on metal parts — no sovereign sets a content maximum, so the 3 mg/kg value is READ ACROSS to them and applied article-wide. The read-across is disclosed and is argued from the material and the contact, not from convenience: it keeps the SAME analyte (Cr(VI) specifically, not total chromium) and the SAME basis (mg/kg of the component's dry mass), and crosses only a material boundary, from chrome-tanned leather to a chromate-pigmented or chromate-passivated surface. The hazard is identical (Cr(VI) skin sensitisation) and the route is identical (dermal transfer under sweat from a surface held against the child), which is exactly why entry 47 was written for skin-contact leather in the first place. Applying it article-wide is deliberate over-compliance and is the same rule this row applies to lead (90 mg/kg applied to a substrate whose own US limit is 100 mg/kg) and to cadmium (75 mg/kg applied to polymer components whose own EU limit is 100 mg/kg); declining to extend it to Cr(VI), the analyte where compliance costs a supplier a change of passivation chemistry, would be selective over-compliance and is not done. The EU RoHS 0.1 % homogeneous-material Cr(VI) value is scoped to electrical and electronic equipment and is over three hundred times more permissive, so it is not used as the read-across source. The EN 71-3 Category I and II Cr(VI) migration values are numerically lower but are leachate limits measuring transfer rather than content, and are excluded by this row's basis guard.

Cr-VI.binding_control: Determined by ISO 17075-1/-2 on every leather and leather-containing component, and by alkaline digestion with ion chromatography and post-column derivatisation (US EPA 3060A / 7199 approach) on chromate-pigmented coatings, chromate conversion coatings and plated metal parts. A leather component above the published value is a direct breach of REACH Annex XVII entry 47; a non-leather component above it breaches the read-across ceiling and triggers supplier corrective action and substitution to trivalent-chromium or chromium-free passivation.

read_across.substantiation: This is the only TOTAL-CONTENT arsenic maximum in the register that reaches a coated children's article. tAs.basis_label: total arsenic content of the coating material and of the accessible component (mg/kg)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes an inorganic-arsenic limit for an infant swing, bouncer or rocker; every arsenic instrument that reaches this category regulates the total element (the Australian coating-content limit adopted for the tAs cell is explicitly an unspeciated arsenic value, and REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 likewise limits arsenic compounds expressed as As metal). Inorganic arsenic is nevertheless NOT declared not-material here, because residual arsenical pigments in coatings, printed fabric and decals, and arsenic carried in recycled-content polymer feedstock is a real inorganic-arsenic pathway in this article class and a not-material determination would be an affirmative claim the material contradicts. The species is therefore held under mandatory analytical control, bounded above by the published total-arsenic ceiling.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-arsenic content screen on every accessible component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS (arsenite and arsenate, after a speciation-preserving extraction) on any component returning total arsenic above the reporting limit. Preservative-treated timber, arsenical pigments and recycled-content polymers are sampled as distinct components. Results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule; inorganic arsenic can never exceed the published total-arsenic ceiling by identity.
