control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a TOTAL-chromium value for an infant blanket, swaddle or wearable sleep sack in this row's extraction basis. REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 regulates chromium(VI) specifically and not total chromium, which is the correct regulatory choice: total chromium in a textile is dominated by benign trivalent chromium from chrome-tanned leather trim, chromium(III) mordants and chromium-complex dyes, while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), and that species carries a firm published 1 mg/kg extractable ceiling on this same row. The Australian coating-content value (60 mg/kg) and the ASTM F963 soluble value (60 mg/kg) sit in other bases. Publishing a total-chromium ceiling would add no protection over the published Cr(VI) ceiling and would misrepresent a benign total as a hazard measure, so total chromium is held as a screening control.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-chromium content screen by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on the base textile, on each dyed and printed component and on any leather or chrome-tanned trim. A total-chromium detection is the trigger for the Cr(VI) determination published on this same row; total chromium itself carries no ceiling and is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule against the supplier's own dye and tanning specification.

Cr-VI.basis_label: extractable element content of the homogeneous textile material after the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 extraction (mg/kg of homogeneous material)
Cr-VI.label: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12: 1 mg/kg chromium(VI) compounds in the homogeneous material after extraction.
Cr-VI.substantiation: Entry 72 Appendix 12 binds an infant blanket, swaddle or wearable sleep sack directly at 1 mg/kg extractable Cr(VI), expressed as Cr(VI). Where the garment or accessory carries a leather part in skin contact, REACH Annex XVII entry 47 additionally binds that part at 3 mg/kg on the total dry weight of the leather — a CONTENT basis on a different measured quantity, enforced as a companion obligation and not merged into the extractable ceiling published here. The EU RoHS 0.1 % homogeneous-material Cr(VI) value is scoped to electrical and electronic equipment and is not applicable.

clasps-fasteners-infant-products.name: Clasps/fasteners (snaps, zippers, buttons) used in infant products
clasps-fasteners-infant-products.native_basis: total element content of the fastener component and of its plating, lacquer or applied coating, as placed on market, expressed as mg/kg of the homogenised component and of the dried non-volatile coating film, determined by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS. This is a CONTENT basis. It is not the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 after-extraction textile basis used for the garment the fastener is attached to, and it is not a nickel-release, toy-migration or food-contact-migration basis.
clasps-fasteners-infant-products.native_basis_label: total element content of the fastener component and its plating or coating (mg/kg of component; dried non-volatile film for platings and lacquers) — a content basis, not an extraction, nickel-release or migration basis
clasps-fasteners-infant-products.scope_note: Metal and plastic snaps, prong and ring sets, zip sliders, pulls, teeth and stops, buttons, rivets, eyelets, D-rings, sliders, buckles, hook-and-loop hardware and decorative metal trim, on any Category 10 product and on any infant garment. The fastener is sampled and certified as its own component precisely because it must NOT be homogenised into the textile extraction sample of the garment it is attached to — a metal snap and a cotton jersey are different homogeneous materials in different bases, and merging them would dilute the metal result and conflate the two bases at once. The dominant health question for this row is allergic nickel release under prolonged skin contact, which is governed by an areal release rate rather than by a content ceiling; see the nickel cell.
clasps-fasteners-infant-products.material: brass, zinc-alloy die-cast, steel and stainless-steel fastener bodies, with nickel, brass, chrome, gold-tone and matte-black electroplated or PVD finishes, baked enamel and lacquer caps, and moulded acetal, nylon and polyester fastener bodies on plastic hardware
clasps-fasteners-infant-products.components: fastener body alloy (each of cap, socket, stud and prong sampled separately for a snap; slider, pull, teeth and stops separately for a zip); electroplated or PVD surface finish; baked enamel, lacquer or printed cap coating; moulded polymer fastener body; any leather or synthetic pull tab — each sampled and digested as a distinct homogeneous component, with the outward-facing plated or coated surface, which is the surface in skin and mouth contact, sampled first
clasps-fasteners-infant-products.audit_scope: children'?s product|consumer product|accessible part|surface coating|sticker, film|painted article|synthetic organic polymer|toys|childcare|skin contact|leather|jewell|jewelry|adornment|metal beads|hair accessor|homogeneous material|mouthable|coated with a material
clasps-fasteners-infant-products.basis_guard: ^(?!.*(migration|migratable|soluble|bioavailable|after extraction|leachate|as consumed|as sold|edible|muscle meat|wet weight|product as placed on market|portion ordinarily consumed))(?=.*(content|paint|surface coating|coating material|plastic material|leather|percent by weight|homogeneous material))
clasps-fasteners-infant-products.basis_guard_note: Drawn at the boundary of the TOTAL-CONTENT family. It admits only register rows whose basis is the mass fraction of the element in a homogenised component, coating film, plastic material or metal part, and rejects every leachate/transfer basis: EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48/EC toy migration, ASTM F963 and NOM-252 soluble/bioavailable elements, GB 21027 migratable content, EU 10/2011 specific migration into food, the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 after-extraction textile basis, and all dietary wet-weight and as-consumed food maximum levels. A migration number is a different measured quantity from a content number and must never be published as one; if a named anchor drifts across the boundary the cell resolves to a GAP and the build fails.

Pb.basis_label: total lead content of the fastener component and of its dried plating, lacquer or coating film (mg/kg)
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-lead content limit for a component of a children's product and for its coating: 90 mg/kg (US 16 CFR 1303; Canada SOR/2018-83 accessible parts; Canada SOR/2016-193 surface coating materials and applied coatings on products for children).
Pb.substantiation: A fastener on an infant product is an accessible part of a children's product and its plating or lacquer is a surface coating material, so all five named instruments reach it directly and the strictest, 90 mg/kg, is published. This matters more here than on any other row in the category: leaded brass and leaded zinc die-cast are the historic failure mode for small metal children's-product components, and the CPSIA 100 mg/kg substrate value is the looser of the two US numbers, so HMTc publishes 90 mg/kg and applies it to the alloy body as well as to the plating. The Canadian children's-jewellery lead limit (SOR/2018-82 s.2, 90 mg/kg) and the Chinese GB 28480 children's-jewellery total-lead value (300 mg/kg) are recorded as near-neighbour instruments; the Canadian value is identical to the published one and the Chinese value is looser, so neither changes the result. The EU REACH Annex XVII entry 63 mouthable-article value (500 mg/kg) and its brass-alloy exception (5 000 mg/kg) are far looser and are not selected — HMTc does not take the brass exception. Companion sub-national obligations, disclosed and not adopted as the anchor: the Washington Children's Safe Product Act (register rows wa_cspa2008_pb_childrens_products_90ppm, s.3(1)(a), and wa_cspa2008_cd_childrens_products_40ppm, s.3(1)(b)) prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 40 mg/kg in a children's product or product component, and Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892 prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 75 mg/kg in covered consumer products. Both are stricter than the adopted cadmium anchor. Neither is selected here because each statute's own product definition is narrower than the CPSIA 'children's product' definition and the register carries only the phrases 'children's products and product components covered by the Washington Children's Safe Product Act' and 'covered consumer products and product components listed in Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892, subject to exceptions', which do not establish whether this product form is inside the covered list. Applicability to the exact cell cannot be resolved from the register, so the rows are published as jurisdiction-specific companion obligations and logged as register gaps for scope-resolved re-ingest rather than selected as the HMTc value.

components.component: moulded polymer fastener body (acetal and nylon buckles, sliders, plastic snaps and buttons)
metal fastener part (brass and zinc-alloy body, plated finish, zip teeth and slider)
baked enamel, lacquer or printed cap coating

component_read_across.basis_label: total cadmium content of the fastener component material (mg/kg of the homogenised component or of the dried coating film)
component_read_across.label: Strictest applicable total-content cadmium limit among this fastener's principal components: the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 coating value of 75 mg/kg on the non-volatile content of the coating material, read across to the enamel and lacquer finishes on fastener caps. HMTc applies the strictest component value to the whole fastener.
component_read_across.substantiation: All three candidates are TOTAL-CONTENT limits, so the strictest-of-components selection compares like with like. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 23 paragraph 1 (100 mg/kg cadmium in articles produced from the listed synthetic organic polymers) binds a moulded acetal or nylon fastener body DIRECTLY. Entry 23 paragraph 10 (100 mg/kg cadmium in metal beads and other metal components for jewellery making, metal parts of jewellery and imitation jewellery, and hair accessories) is READ ACROSS to a metal snap, zip or button: a fastener is not jewellery, but it is the same class of small plated metal component worn against a child's skin all day, and it is the nearest sovereign cadmium content limit for that component. The Australian coating value (75 mg/kg) is read across from coated toys to the enamel and lacquer on a fastener cap, and being the strictest of the three it becomes the published ceiling for the whole fastener. Near-neighbour instruments recorded and not selected: Canada SOR/2018-82 s.3 (130 mg/kg cadmium in small children's jewellery) is looser; Connecticut PA 10-113 and Minnesota Ch. 347 (75 mg/kg in children's jewellery) are sub-national and jewellery-scoped, the Minnesota value additionally sitting in a soluble basis; California SB 929 (300 mg/kg) is looser. Companion sub-national obligations, disclosed and not adopted as the anchor: the Washington Children's Safe Product Act (register rows wa_cspa2008_pb_childrens_products_90ppm, s.3(1)(a), and wa_cspa2008_cd_childrens_products_40ppm, s.3(1)(b)) prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 40 mg/kg in a children's product or product component, and Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892 prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 75 mg/kg in covered consumer products. Both are stricter than the adopted cadmium anchor. Neither is selected here because each statute's own product definition is narrower than the CPSIA 'children's product' definition and the register carries only the phrases 'children's products and product components covered by the Washington Children's Safe Product Act' and 'covered consumer products and product components listed in Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892, subject to exceptions', which do not establish whether this product form is inside the covered list. Applicability to the exact cell cannot be resolved from the register, so the rows are published as jurisdiction-specific companion obligations and logged as register gaps for scope-resolved re-ingest rather than selected as the HMTc value.

read_across.label: Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 item 2: 25 mg/kg arsenic in the non-volatile content of coating material on a coated toy, read across to the enamel, lacquer and plated finishes on an infant-product fastener.
read_across.substantiation: This is the only TOTAL-CONTENT arsenic maximum in the register that reaches a coated children's article. The instrument records arsenic as an unspecified species, so it is published on tAs and never on iAs. Arsenic is a recognised residual in brass and zinc-alloy feedstock and in some plating baths, which is why the value is applied to the alloy body as well as to the coating. The ASTM F963 (25 mg/kg) and Chinese GB 28480 children's-jewellery (25 mg/kg) arsenic values are numerically identical but sit in soluble-element leachate bases and are excluded by this row's basis guard.

tAs.basis_label: total arsenic content of the fastener component and of its coating (mg/kg)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes an inorganic-arsenic limit for a snap, zip, button, buckle, rivet, eyelet or other clasp or fastener on an infant product; every arsenic instrument that reaches this category regulates the total element (the Australian coating-content limit adopted for the tAs cell is explicitly an unspeciated arsenic value, and REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 likewise limits arsenic compounds expressed as As metal). Inorganic arsenic is nevertheless NOT declared not-material here, because residual arsenic in brass and zinc-alloy feedstock and in electroplating bath chemistry is a real inorganic-arsenic pathway in this article class and a not-material determination would be an affirmative claim the material contradicts. The species is therefore held under mandatory analytical control, bounded above by the published total-arsenic ceiling.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-arsenic content screen on every accessible component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS (arsenite and arsenate, after a speciation-preserving extraction) on any component returning total arsenic above the reporting limit. Preservative-treated timber, arsenical pigments and recycled-content polymers are sampled as distinct components. Results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule; inorganic arsenic can never exceed the published total-arsenic ceiling by identity.

tHg.basis_label: total mercury content of a dried sample of the plating, lacquer or coating on the fastener (mg/kg)
tHg.label: Canada Surface Coating Materials Regulations SOR/2016-193 s.5: not more than 10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried sample of surface coating material.
tHg.substantiation: The instrument's register scope is 'surface coating material' with no product qualifier, so it binds the plating, lacquer, enamel and printed finish on a fastener DIRECTLY. HMTc applies it to the fastener alloy body as well as to the finish. The Chinese GB 28480 metal-adornment total-mercury value (1 000 mg/kg) and the children's-jewellery soluble value (60 mg/kg) are looser and, in the second case, in a different basis; neither is selected.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a marine-bioaccumulation species. It has no formation route and no established industrial source in a snap, zip, button, buckle, rivet, eyelet or other clasp or fastener on an infant product: the mercury that can occur here comes from pigment, catalyst and preservative residues in coatings, polymers and dyestuffs, all of which are inorganic or aryl-mercury chemistries, and organomercury fungicides in these materials have been withdrawn across every jurisdiction checked. Every sovereign mercury instrument that reaches this article class is written on TOTAL mercury; not one sets a methylmercury value for an article, a coating or a textile. Methylmercury is a proper subset of total mercury by identity, so the published 10 mg/kg total-mercury coating ceiling on this row bounds it absolutely and a separate methylmercury ceiling would add no protection.
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury content screen by microwave-assisted acid digestion with CV-AFS or ICP-MS on every accessible component, with reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS reserved for any component that both exceeds the total-mercury reporting limit and carries a declared organomercury input. No routine methylmercury determination is required.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for an article, a surface coating or a textile. The mercury instruments that reach this category are Canada SOR/2016-193 s.5 (10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried sample of surface coating material), Canada SOR/2011-17 s.23(1)(c) (10 mg/kg total mercury in accessible toy coatings), the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 toy-coating value (60 mg/kg, unspeciated) and Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III (total-mercury migration) — all total-element.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (REACH Annex XVII entries 23, 27, 47, 63, 72; Directive 2009/48/EC; Directive 2011/65/EU RoHS; Regulation 10/2011), US (CPSIA s.101, 16 CFR 1303, ASTM F963 via CPSIA s.106), Canada (SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-82, SOR/2018-83, SOR/2011-17), Australia (Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2), UK, Codex — register-checked, no methylmercury row for any article, coating or textile scope.
not_material.substantiation: Bounded by the total-mercury cell on this same row, which is a published sovereign value in the row's own native basis, so the not-material determination is a speciation bound against a real ceiling rather than an assertion of absence.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a nickel CONTENT maximum for a snap, zip, button, buckle, rivet, eyelet or other clasp or fastener on an infant product. The governing instrument for the actual hazard — allergic contact dermatitis from prolonged skin contact with plated snaps, zip sliders and teeth, rivets, eyelets and buckle hardware held against the skin for the whole wearing period — is the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 nickel-release restriction, which is expressed as an areal release rate (µg/cm² per week) and therefore cannot be expressed in this register's µg/kg content unit; it is not present in the register in any form. The EN 71-3 toy nickel migration values and the EU 10/2011 nickel specific-migration value both sit in leachate bases outside this row's native basis. No number is invented: the cell is held under mandatory analytical control.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-nickel content analysis of every accessible metal, plated and alloy component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, plus EN 1811 nickel-release testing (with EN 12472 wear-and-corrosion pre-treatment for coated or plated parts) on every component in prolonged skin contact, dispositioned against the release criterion in the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 restriction as a companion conformity obligation. That criterion's numeric value is deliberately NOT reproduced here: the restriction is absent from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and this standard quotes no number that is not carried by a named register row. The criterion is applied from the instrument text at audit and is logged as a register gap for ingest through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway. Any component exceeding the release criterion, or any total-nickel result that is an outlier against the supplier's own qualification data, triggers supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a total-tin content maximum for a snap, zip, button, buckle, rivet, eyelet or other clasp or fastener on an infant product. The instrument that does reach this article class — REACH Annex XVII entry 20, which covers textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, childcare articles and other consumer articles in skin contact — restricts ORGANOTIN (dibutyltin and dioctyltin) expressed as tin at 0.1 % by weight. Organotin expressed as tin is a different measurand from total tin: publishing 1 000 mg/kg as this row's total-tin ceiling would pass off a speciated restriction as a total-element limit. The organotin restriction is therefore carried as a companion obligation and no total-tin number is invented. This row DOES read a value across for hexavalent chromium, and the difference is principled rather than convenient: the chromium read-across crosses only a MATERIAL boundary while holding the analyte and the basis fixed, whereas an organotin read-across would cross an ANALYTE boundary, publishing a speciated restriction as a total-element ceiling. A material boundary can be crossed with disclosure; an analyte boundary cannot be crossed at all.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-tin content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with reflex organotin speciation by GC-ICP-MS (dibutyltin, dioctyltin, tributyltin, triphenyltin) on any component returning total tin above the reporting limit. Speciated results are dispositioned against the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 0.1 %-as-tin companion criterion; total-tin results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule against the tightest available supplier qualification context.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes an aluminium content maximum for a snap, zip, button, buckle, rivet, eyelet or other clasp or fastener on an infant product. Aluminium is a structural alloy in this category — frames, tubing, folding mechanisms, rivets and buckle bodies are routinely aluminium by design — so a content ceiling on the homogenised component is not a meaningful contamination control and no sovereign has set one. The EN 71-3 Category III aluminium migration value (28 130 mg/kg) and the EU 10/2011 aluminium specific-migration value (1 mg/kg into food) are leachate limits in other bases and are not read across into a content ceiling. No number is invented.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total-aluminium content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on every non-structural accessible component (coatings, plastics, textiles, foams, printed decals), with structural aluminium alloy components identified and dispositioned by declared alloy specification rather than by a contamination ceiling. Aluminium detected in a component whose declared composition contains no aluminium is treated as a contamination signal and escalated to supplier corrective action.

read_across.label: Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 item 2: 60 mg/kg chromium in the non-volatile content of coating material on a coated toy, read across to the plated, enamelled and lacquered finishes on an infant-product fastener. Reported as a SCREEN.
read_across.substantiation: The instrument records chromium as an unspecified species and the register maps it to total chromium. On a plated fastener the total is dominated by trivalent chromium from decorative chrome and chromium(III) conversion coatings, so the value is recorded as a screen rather than as a protective ceiling; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI) and is dispositioned on this row's Cr-VI control. The ASTM F963 total-chromium value (60 mg/kg) and the Chinese GB 28480 children's-jewellery soluble value (60 mg/kg) sit in leachate bases and are excluded by this row's basis guard.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is a screen cell, not a firm protective ceiling: on a plated fastener the measured total is dominated by trivalent chromium from decorative chrome and chromium(III) conversion coatings, while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). A total-chromium result at or below 60 mg/kg does not by itself demonstrate Cr(VI) compliance, and any total-chromium detection is the trigger for the Cr(VI) determination on this same row.
Cr.basis_label: total chromium content of the fastener component and of its plating or coating (mg/kg)

read_across.label: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 47 paragraphs 5 and 6 (Regulation (EU) No 301/2014): 3 mg/kg hexavalent chromium on the total dry weight of leather, for leather articles and articles containing leather parts coming into contact with the skin. Applied article-wide.
read_across.substantiation: This is the only hexavalent-chromium CONTENT limit in the register that reaches a skin-contact article, and it binds DIRECTLY wherever a snap, zip, button, buckle, rivet, eyelet or other clasp or fastener on an infant product carries a leather part in skin contact — a leather handlebar or bumper-bar wrap, a harness pad, a leather trim panel or a leather pull tab. For the article's non-leather Cr(VI) pathways — chromate-pigmented coatings, chromate conversion coatings and hexavalent chrome plating on metal parts — no sovereign sets a content maximum, so the 3 mg/kg value is READ ACROSS to them and applied article-wide. The read-across is disclosed and is argued from the material and the contact, not from convenience: it keeps the SAME analyte (Cr(VI) specifically, not total chromium) and the SAME basis (mg/kg of the component's dry mass), and crosses only a material boundary, from chrome-tanned leather to a chromate-pigmented or chromate-passivated surface. The hazard is identical (Cr(VI) skin sensitisation) and the route is identical (dermal transfer under sweat from a surface held against the child), which is exactly why entry 47 was written for skin-contact leather in the first place. Applying it article-wide is deliberate over-compliance and is the same rule this row applies to lead (90 mg/kg applied to a substrate whose own US limit is 100 mg/kg) and to cadmium (75 mg/kg applied to polymer components whose own EU limit is 100 mg/kg); declining to extend it to Cr(VI), the analyte where compliance costs a supplier a change of passivation chemistry, would be selective over-compliance and is not done. The EU RoHS 0.1 % homogeneous-material Cr(VI) value is scoped to electrical and electronic equipment and is over three hundred times more permissive, so it is not used as the read-across source. The EN 71-3 Category I and II Cr(VI) migration values are numerically lower but are leachate limits measuring transfer rather than content, and are excluded by this row's basis guard.

Cr-VI.basis_label: hexavalent chromium content on the total dry weight of the component (mg/kg) — leather, coating film, or plated and conversion-coated metal part
Cr-VI.binding_control: Determined by ISO 17075-1/-2 on every leather and leather-containing component, and by alkaline digestion with ion chromatography and post-column derivatisation (US EPA 3060A / 7199 approach) on chromate-pigmented coatings, chromate conversion coatings and plated metal parts. A leather component above the published value is a direct breach of REACH Annex XVII entry 47; a non-leather component above it breaches the read-across ceiling and triggers supplier corrective action and substitution to trivalent-chromium or chromium-free passivation.
